steps.say: Traumatic brain injury is graded by the Glasgow Coma Scale into mild, moderate and severe bands that decide scan with admission with intensive care. Mild injury is scored thirteen to fifteen, moderate nine to twelve, and severe eight or below. The scale sums eye with verbal with motor responses, and the motor score carries the most prognosis. Scoring is repeated because a falling score means a growing bleed.
steps.tx: **TBI severity** follows the **Glasgow Coma Scale**: mild **13 to 15**, moderate **9 to 12**, severe **8 or below**. The scale sums **eye, verbal and motor** responses; motor carries most prognosis. A **falling score** means a growing bleed and triggers rescan. **Severe** injury needs intubation with pressure control.

steps.say: Primary injury happens at impact and cannot be undone, while secondary injury from low pressure with low oxygen with swelling is preventable. Hypotension with hypoxia doubles death, so both are corrected before the scanner. Fluids with oxygen with transfusion targets are set early. The golden hour is really about pressure with oxygen, not speed alone.
steps.tx: **Primary injury** occurs at impact and is fixed; **secondary injury** from hypotension, hypoxia and swelling is preventable. **Hypotension with hypoxia** doubles death and is corrected first. **Systolic pressure** targets with oxygen saturation targets are set early. **Tranexamic acid** within three hours limits bleeding in mild to moderate injury.

steps.say: An extradural haematoma classically knocks out, wakes up, then collapses again as the middle meningeal artery bleeds. The lucid interval is the warning that fools bystanders, and the pupil blows on the same side as the clot. Computed tomography shows a lens shaped collection that does not cross sutures. Clots above thirty millilitres with coma are evacuated at once.
steps.tx: **Extradural haematoma** gives knock out, **lucid interval**, then collapse from **middle meningeal** bleeding. The pupil blows **ipsilaterally**. **CT** shows a lens shaped clot that **does not cross sutures**. Evacuate when volume exceeds **30 mL** or coma deepens. **Subdural** clots are crescentic and cross sutures.

points: Lens shaped, lucid interval, artery bleed
left.title: Extradural

steps.say: Concussion needs no scan when the picture is classic, but it needs respect because second impact kills. Headache with fog with imbalance after a knock with no red flags is managed with a day of relative rest. Return to play climbs stepwise over days, and any worsening restarts the ladder. Repeated concussions end seasons, and schooling is adjusted meanwhile.
steps.tx: **Concussion** needs no scan without red flags: headache, fog and imbalance after a knock get **relative rest** for a day. **Graduated return** climbs stepwise; worsening restarts the ladder. **Second impact** before recovery kills. **Repeat concussions** end seasons. **Schooling** is adjusted till symptoms clear.

steps.say: Diffuse axonal injury shears the white matter in high speed crashes and leaves coma with a normal scan. Tiny bleeds at grey white junctions with corpus callosum with brainstem show on susceptibility sequences days later. Recovery stretches over months with agitation with amnesia, and prognosis is guarded. Seat belts with helmets prevent most cases, which is the public health message attached to every discharge.
steps.tx: **Diffuse axonal injury** shears white matter in high speed crashes: **coma with near normal CT**. **Susceptibility MRI** shows grey white junction bleeds days later. Recovery spans months with agitation and amnesia. **Seat belts and helmets** prevent most cases. **Prognosis** stays guarded despite normal pressure.

steps.say: Raised pressure is lowered in a fixed ladder, and each rung is exhausted before the next. The head is raised with sedation with drainage through a ventricular catheter, then hypertonic saline pulls water from the brain. Barbiturate coma with cooling follows refractory surges, and decompressive craniectomy removes the bone flap as the last resort. Pupils with pressure numbers guide every step.
steps.tx: **ICP ladder** runs fixed rungs: **head up, sedate, drain CSF**, then **hypertonic saline** for surges. **Barbiturate coma** with cooling follows refractory pressure. **Decompressive craniectomy** removes bone as last resort. **Pupils with pressure readings** guide each rung; fixed dilated pupil means herniation.

steps.say: Early seizures within a week are prevented with a short course of antiseizure drugs, and levetiracetam is the usual choice. Late epilepsy needs long term treatment once two unprovoked seizures occur. Phenytoin loads faster in status but interacts widely, so levetiracetam leads in most units. Alcohol withdrawal is excluded in every fit, because it mimics and multiplies trauma seizures.
steps.tx: **Early post-traumatic seizures** (within a week) are prevented with a short **levetiracetam** course. **Late epilepsy** needs long term drugs after two unprovoked fits. **Phenytoin** loads in status but interacts widely. **Alcohol withdrawal** is excluded in every fit as it mimics trauma seizures.

steps.say: Spinal cord injury is immobilised at the scene with a hard collar, and the collar stays till the spine is cleared. High lesions paralyse breathing with blood pressure, so ventilation with vasopressors starts early. Mean pressure is kept high for a week to perfuse the cord, and steroids are no longer given routinely. Bedsores with clots with bladder harm are prevented from day one.
steps.tx: **Spinal injury** is **immobilised** with a collar till cleared. **High lesions** need ventilation with vasopressors. **Mean pressure** is kept high for a week to perfuse the cord. **Steroids are not routine** anymore. **Clots, sores and bladder** harm are prevented from day one with heparin, turns and catheters.

steps.say: Every head injury follows the same imaging rules, and scanning too little kills while scanning everything wastes. Canadian C T rules with N E X U S are used to clear the head with the neck clinically in mild cases. Vomiting twice with amnesia with dangerous mechanism earns a scan. The neck is cleared with computed tomography when pain persists, and collars stay till then.
steps.tx: **CT rules** decide scans: **Canadian head rules** (vomiting twice, amnesia, dangerous mechanism) and **NEXUS** for the neck. **Skull signs** (panda eyes, Battle sign, CSF leak) force scanning. **C spine CT** clears persistent neck pain. **Collars stay** till clearance; clearing clinically needs a sober alert patient.

steps.say: Outcome follows the motor score with pupil response with scan findings, and the young recover beyond every prediction. Post concussion symptoms fade within three months in most, while severe injury leaves personality change with epilepsy with dependence. Rehabilitation with seizure watch with mood care runs for years. Helmets with belts with drink limits prevent more disability than any intensive care unit.
steps.tx: **Prognosis** follows **motor score, pupils and CT**: young brains recover beyond prediction. **Post-concussion** symptoms fade within three months mostly. **Severe injury** leaves personality change, epilepsy and dependence. **Rehab with mood care** runs years. **Helmets, belts and drink limits** prevent more harm than any unit.

steps.say: For the exam, the facts to lock in are thirteen to fifteen mild with eight or below severe, lucid interval for extradural, crescent crossing sutures for subdural, hypertonic saline for surges, levetiracetam for early fits, and collar till cleared. Tranexamic acid runs within three hours and steroids are not routine in cord injury. Memorise the facts in this table exactly as written.
steps.tx: **High yield for the exam:** GCS **13 to 15** is mild, **8 or below** severe. **Lucid interval** marks extradural; **crescent crossing sutures** marks subdural. **Hypertonic saline** treats surges. **Levetiracetam** prevents early fits. **Tranexamic** runs within three hours. **Collar** stays till spine cleared.
